title: One marked holding, one failed run, no recorded orders

One marked holding, one failed run, no recorded orders

Paper trading · 2026-10-28T17:00:19.626133-04:00

At the 2026-10-28 21:00:19 UTC cutoff, the paper account showed $2,000 cash and equity. The mean-reversion book had one MU holding, valued using a $981.47 midpoint observed at 20:00:00 UTC (4:00 p.m. EDT), before the report cutoff. That snapshot is not a live price. The supplied records show no proposal, risk approval or rejection, submitted order, or actual broker or simulated fill for today. A scheduled research run failed because its planner context exceeded a configured limit; it is a failure, not a completed decision or deliberate wait.

Today's lesson: A snapshot gain is not a completed sale

A marked gain is not the same as booked profit. For MU, 0.053191 shares times the $41.59 difference between the observed price ($981.47) and average purchase price ($939.88) gives about $2.21 unrealized gain. The book summary still reports $0 realized P&L, and its gain excludes fees.

What the activity records establish

The paper account and the simulated books are separate records. No broker fill or simulated fill is shown for October 28, and a submitted order would not by itself establish a fill. The records supplied here also do not show a completed deterministic risk evaluation, so whether any proposal would have been approved or rejected is unknown.

Reading the book snapshot

The MU quote was observed at 20:00:00 UTC, while the report cutoff was 21:00:19 UTC. The book's cash replay plus holding mark totals $2,002.21. This snapshot-based total can differ from a live valuation, and the supplied prices and gains exclude fees.

What to watch next

Watch whether a later scheduled run completes and what it records: any proposal, deterministic risk result, submission, and fill should be read as separate steps. For MU, note the observation time alongside any newer recorded price.

Mark: A recorded estimate of a holding's value at a stated observation time. Here, the book used the recorded bid/ask midpoint, not a guaranteed live quote.

Unrealized gain or loss: Gain or loss on a holding that remains open, based on its recorded value and purchase basis. It is not the same as realized P&L.

Data timing and limitations

Prices come from recorded snapshots, not a guaranteed closing-price feed.
Paper account holdings use the latest recorded snapshot, which may precede fills.
Book marks use observed bid/ask midpoints at price_as_of, not guaranteed live prices. Without an admitted quote the value remains unknown; book gains exclude fees.
Work starting after the cutoff is outside this report. Failures remain labelled.
